messages:
Jordan (Customer): Hey — hitting handshake failures when our service calls our Redwood Private endpoint through our corporate TLS proxy. Started ~09:00 UTC. curl returns: "curl: (35) SSL: no shared cipher" and some apps show "sslv3 alert handshake failure"
Maya (Support): Sorry about that. Can you paste the exact curl/openssl output and which proxy appliance/version you're using?
Jordan (Customer): curl -v https://private.redwood.example.com/api/v1/health
* SSL connection using TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood.example.com/api/v1/health
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, handshake failure (592):
* error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure
curl: (35) SSL: no shared cipher
We run BlueGate Proxy v8.1.
Maya (Support): Thanks — can you run and paste this too (redact certs):
```
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood.example.com
```
Jordan (Customer): Paste below:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood.example.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
139731112345600:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s23_clnt.c:770:
no peer certificate
---
Cipher is (NONE)
---
```
Maya (Support): That "Cipher is (NONE)" + "handshake failure" usually means the proxy and the backend don't share any cipher suites. Can you ask the proxy team for the allowed TLS protocol versions + cipher list?
Jordan (Customer): Asked them — they replied: corporate policy enforces TLSv1.2 only and the cipher suite list is RSA-only: `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` (no ECDSA/ECDHE-ECDSA suites enabled).
Samir P (Eng): That explains it. Our Private endpoint is configured with an ECDSA leaf cert (we opted for ECDSA for perf/size) and by default only advertises ECDHE-ECDSA AES-GCM suites. If the proxy only allows RSA-keyed suites there is zero overlap -> handshake fails.
Aleks (Network): BlueGate's default profile for some orgs is RSA-only for legacy compatibility. We can add ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 to the allowed list, or configure SNI passthrough so the proxy doesn't terminate TLS. Which is preferred?
Jordan (Customer): Our security team is strict about cipher changes; they prefer not to relax the proxy profile unless absolutely necessary. Is there something Redwood can do on your side?
Samir P (Eng): Options: 1) We issue an RSA cert for your Private endpoint so the proxy's RSA-only list can negotiate; 2) Your proxy allows at least ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256/TLS1.2; 3) Configure the proxy to do TLS passthrough for that hostname (SNI/TCP passthrough). We usually recommend option 2 or 3. Option 1 is possible as a short-term workaround but requires cert rollout on our side.
Clara (SRE): If you need a quick fix, we can generate an RSA leaf cert and deploy to your endpoint — it's a cert swap and shouldn't need infra changes. We'll need your confirmation and a short maintenance window (10-20 minutes) to rotate. Longer-term, enabling ECDSA+RSA on the LB is preferable so both legacy proxies and modern ones work.
Jordan (Customer): Security team hates changing proxy cipher policy. They said they can do passthrough for specific hosts if necessary. Can you share an example nginx stream config to passthrough SNI?
Maya (Support): Example nginx stream passthrough (replace host/ports):
```
stream {
  upstream redwood_backend {
    server private.redwood.example.com:443;
  }
  server {
    listen 443;
    proxy_pass redwood_backend;
    ssl_preread on; # allows SNI-based routing without terminating TLS
  }
}
```
Maya (Support): If you go this route the proxy will not inspect/terminate TLS and the backend certs remain end-to-end.
Aleks (Network): For BlueGate UI the change is: Security -> SSL Profiles -> Edit Cipher Suites -> add `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256` and enable TLS1.2/TLS1.3 if policy allows. We can propose that to security as a scoped exception.
Jordan (Customer): Security still prefers no cipher changes. They asked if Redwood can issue RSA cert. If you can do that fast we'll take it.
Clara (SRE): We can issue RSA cert for this hostname as a temporary measure. Need approval from product to proceed (impact low). ETA ~2 hours including validation and rotation.
Maya (Support): Escalating to product for sign-off. I'll update this thread once approved.
deploy-bot: Certificate rotation job queued for private.redwood.example.com (job id #6421).
Maya (Support): Product approved — proceeding with RSA cert swap. Will post when rotated.
deploy-bot: Certificate rotation completed successfully for private.redwood.example.com (job id #6421).
Jordan (Customer): Re-tested from behind the corp proxy — calls are now succeeding, no handshake errors. Thanks!
Clara (SRE): Great — sounds resolved. Long-term we recommend enabling ECDSA ciphers or passthrough. Happy to re-open if anything else shows up. :tada:
